source_snapshot.purpose_facts: Record CPU name, core quantity, speed and cache in Linux and GNOME System Monitor, then compare with CPU specification.
procedure_facts: Run `cat /proc/cpuinfo` and inspect GNOME System Monitor.
criteria_facts: CPU information matches the provided specification.
missing_source_information: Approved CPU/socket/topology/base-turbo/cache specification and allowed OS reservations/offline CPUs.
Definition of core quantity and speed/cache comparison semantics.

original_test_intent.statement: Collect Linux-visible CPU identity, physical/logical topology, frequency and cache information and compare it with the approved CPU specification; GUI evidence is corroborative, not a different test.
must_preserve: CPU name, cores, speed and cache in Linux.
must_not_infer: A sampled MHz value as rated base/maximum frequency.
Cache totals without socket/core sharing context.

v2_review_conclusion.summary: V2 correctly replaces nonessential GUI observation with complete secure CLI evidence and retains human specification judgment.
v2_review_conclusion.specific_gap: V2 does not explicitly separate sockets/cores/threads and online/offline CPUs, current/base/max frequency, or per-level cache size and sharing domains, which can create false mismatches.

related_records: No GUI-only requirement prevents equivalent Linux CLI collection.
applicable_history.precedence_application: Source intent is information equivalence; CLI can satisfy it without claiming GUI observation.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Safe read-only collection is ready; comparison awaits the approved CPU specification. Actual data can be collected now without claiming PASS.

conditions_present: Linux exposes cpuinfo/sysfs/lscpu data and collection is read-only.
missing: Expected socket/core/thread, CPU model/stepping, frequency/cache values and allowed offline/reserved-core policy.
provider: Platform/CPU owner supplies the approved specification and deviations.
safe_read_only_work: Collect full `lscpu -e`, `lscpu`, `/proc/cpuinfo`, online/offline sysfs CPU sets, cpufreq policy values and cache topology.
prohibited_until_resolved: Changing governors/online state, clearing logs or declaring PASS without spec.
closure_evidence: Field-level mapping of measured identity/topology/frequency/cache to the signed specification.

revision_candidate.test_name: Verify Linux CPU Identity, Topology, Frequency and Cache
revision_candidate.purpose: Collect complete Linux CPU identity, socket/core/thread topology, online state, frequency capabilities and cache hierarchy, then compare each field with the approved CPU specification.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The booted Linux OS/kernel on the exact SUT BIOS/CPU population. Intel/AMD topology/frequency reporting differences and virtualization/container restrictions must be recorded.
revision_candidate.target_scope: All installed sockets and Linux-visible logical CPUs, including offline/reserved CPUs and cache sharing domains. No stress or governor change.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Approved CPU SKU/socket/stepping, sockets, cores/socket, threads/core, expected online policy, base/max frequency interpretation, cache levels/sizes/sharing and allowed firmware/OS deviations.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Using authenticated read-only access, record full `lscpu` and extended CPU rows, `/proc/cpuinfo`, sysfs online/offline/present/possible sets, cpufreq policy/driver values where exposed, and per-index cache level/type/size/shared CPU list. Do not reduce output with `head`; correlate IDs to sockets/cores/NUMA and compare field by field.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Linux booted normally; access can read proc/sysfs; CPU hotplug/tuning is stable; specification version identified.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Host/kernel/BIOS identity; raw commands/output; CPU vendor/family/model/stepping/name; socket/core/thread and NUMA map; present/possible/online/offline sets; current sampled and policy base/max frequency with missing fields noted; cache level/type/size/sharing; comparison table; logs and timestamps.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: Signed platform CPU specification and approved BIOS/OS policy. Pass requires all populated CPUs/topology/cache/frequency-capability fields match or have approved deviations; current MHz fluctuation alone is not failure.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Do not change governors, online state, affinity, BIOS, microcode or load; use insecure credentials; truncate output; equate logical CPUs with cores; or claim PASS without expected values.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: No approval for read-only collection; platform engineer approves specification/deviation and final disposition.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: GUI is optional corroboration. Agent may collect CLI evidence; engineer judges spec match.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: None for read-only commands; if a command unexpectedly changes state, stop and preserve evidence.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Wrong host, unstable hotplug/topology, required data inaccessible, specification ambiguous/contradictory or collected fields cannot be mapped reliably.

identified_defects: Core quantity is not defined as physical versus logical.
CPU speed/cache semantics can be misread from cpuinfo.
reason_for_change: Prevent dynamic Linux presentation values from being compared as static SKU facts while retaining fully automated read-only evidence collection.

new_technical_evidence.title: Linux CPU topology
new_technical_evidence.supports: Physical package/core/thread and online topology must be interpreted from topology data rather than processor count alone.

removed_ambiguities: Separates sockets, cores, threads and online state.
resolved_blockers: GUI is not a blocker; safe actuals can be collected before spec arrives.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 prevents three common false mismatches—logical CPUs counted as cores, transient MHz treated as rated speed, and shared cache multiplied per thread—while keeping the case fully read-only and automatable.

agent_understanding_result.notes: Read-only scope is explicit; no DUT validation.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: Compatibility row 24 requests Linux CPU name, core quantity, speed and cache plus GUI corroboration.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 supports CLI equivalence; V3 adds topology/frequency/cache semantic safeguards.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Collect actuals now; no state changes or PASS until spec mapping.
